title: Pharyngeal Anatomy and Waldeyer Ring

steps.tx: At the crossroads where breathed air and swallowed food both enter, a ring of lymphoid tissue stands guard: the adenoid sits above, two palatine tonsils flank the sides, tubal tonsils and the lingual tonsil complete the circuit below. This **Waldeyer ring** samples antigens throughout childhood, which is why its parts enlarge and infect so readily at that age. Neither the adenoid nor the lingual component carries a complete outer capsule.
steps.say: Lymphoid tissue circles the throat entry where air and food passages cross each other. The adenoid is above, the palatine tonsils are at the sides and the lingual tonsil is below. Childhood antigen sampling explains why these structures enlarge and infect so commonly.

steps.tx: The pharynx divides into nasopharynx behind the nose, oropharynx behind the mouth and laryngopharynx above the larynx, each with distinct walls, contents and cancer behaviour. The **nasopharynx** holds the adenoid, Eustachian tube openings and the fossa of Rosenmuller behind each tube, the commonest site of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Boundaries matter because tumours declare themselves by which neighbouring structure they invade first.
steps.say: Three stacked divisions run behind nose, mouth and larynx with distinct contents each. The recess behind each ear tube opening is the commonest nasopharyngeal cancer origin site. Neighbour invasion patterns reveal tumour origin during staging assessment clinically.

steps.tx: **Passavant ridge** is a transverse muscular shelf raised by palatopharyngeus fibres on the posterior pharyngeal wall that meets the soft palate during swallowing and speech, sealing the nasopharynx from the oropharynx. Failure of this velopharyngeal closure produces nasal regurgitation and hypernasal speech, seen after cleft palate repair or palatal paralysis. Videofluoroscopy and nasendoscopy grade the gap before corrective surgery is planned.
steps.say: A muscular shelf rises to meet the soft palate, sealing the nose during swallowing and speech. Closure failure causes nasal regurgitation with hypernasal speech quality in affected patients. Endoscopy and swallow imaging grade the gap before corrective surgery.

steps.tx: **Killian dehiscence** is the weak triangular area between the oblique thyropharyngeus and transverse cricopharyngeus parts of inferior constrictor at the pharyngo-oesophageal junction. Pharyngeal pouches herniate through this gap, and the cricopharyngeus itself forms the upper oesophageal sphincter whose failure contributes to dysphagia. The same constrictor stack, superior middle and inferior, overlaps like stacked flowerpots to propel the bolus downward.
steps.say: A weak triangle between constrictor parts lets pharyngeal pouches herniate outward posteriorly. Muscle below that gap forms the upper gullet sphincter controlling bolus entry onwards. Stacked constrictors overlap like flowerpots to propel food downward sequentially.

steps.tx: Food leaving the oropharynx is funnelled through the piriform fossae, recesses on either side of the laryngeal inlet, and the internal laryngeal nerve lies under that mucosa. Below, **Killian dehiscence** is the weak triangle between the oblique thyropharyngeus and the transverse cricopharyngeus parts of the inferior constrictor. Pouches herniate there. The cricopharyngeus is the upper oesophageal sphincter, and failure of that sphincter adds to dysphagia. Superior, middle, and inferior constrictors overlap like stacked flowerpots to drive the bolus down.
steps.say: Each piriform fossa lies beside the laryngeal inlet and guides the bolus toward the oesophagus, with the internal laryngeal nerve under the mucosa. Farther down, a weak triangle between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus lets a pharyngeal pouch herniate. The cricopharyngeus is the upper oesophageal sphincter. Overlapping constrictors push the bolus onward like stacked flowerpots.

vis.alt: A lateral view of the piriform fossa beside the laryngeal inlet, guiding food toward the oesophagus over the internal laryngeal nerve.
vis.caption: The piriform recess flanks the laryngeal inlet and channels the bolus downward across mucosa that covers the internal laryngeal nerve. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The **piriform fossa** is the recess on each side of the laryngeal inlet that funnels food toward the oesophagus and traps sharp foreign bodies such as fish bones above the cricopharyngeal sphincter. Beneath its mucosa runs the internal laryngeal nerve, so foreign body removal with forceful instrumentation risks sensory loss and aspiration. Deep tumours here stay silent until nodal metastasis declares them, earning the sinus its sinister reputation.
steps.say: Recesses flanking the larynx funnel food toward the gullet while trapping sharp fish bones commonly. Sensory nerves run beneath the lining, so forceful removal risks aspiration afterwards. Silent tumours here present through neck nodes before local symptoms appear.

steps.tx: The **parapharyngeal space** is an inverted pyramid beside the pharynx containing fat, the carotid sheath contents laterally and deep lobe parotid medially, so tumours here displace the tonsil and lateral pharyngeal wall inward. The retropharyngeal space behind the pharynx and the midline danger space behind it conduct infections downward to the mediastinum. Imaging separates these compartments because surgical approach and urgency differ completely between them.
steps.say: A fat filled pyramid beside the throat displaces the tonsil inward when tumours grow there. Infection behind the pharynx leads downward toward the chest cavity along midline planes. Imaging separates these compartments because approach and urgency differ completely.

steps.tx: **Tonsillar blood supply** arrives chiefly from the facial artery tonsillar branch, supplemented by ascending pharyngeal, lingual dorsal, greater palatine and ascending palatine contributions, which explains brisk bleeding when the lower pole is cut. The external palatine or paratonsillar vein descends over the capsule and is the classic source of troublesome primary haemorrhage at tonsillectomy. Venous drainage reaches the pharyngeal plexus and facial vein onward to the internal jugular system.
steps.say: Five arterial contributions supply the tonsil, led by the facial artery branch entering below. A vein descending over the capsule causes classic troublesome bleeding during tonsil surgery characteristically. Blood drains from there to the pharyngeal plexus and the internal jugular vein.

steps.tx: The **sinus of Morgagni** is the gap between the superior constrictor and the skull base, closed only by pharyngobasilar fascia, through which the Eustachian tube and levator palati pass. It is the weak route by which nasopharyngeal tumours escape the pharynx toward the middle cranial structures. Below, the pharyngeal wall layers run mucosa, fascia, muscle and buccopharyngeal fascia from inside outward, the planes abscesses and tumours follow.
steps.say: A fascial gap between upper constrictor and skull base gives passage to the ear tube and a palate muscle. This weak route gives tumours access to cranial structures above the pharynx. The layered wall gives abscesses a predictable route for downward spread.

steps.tx: Lymphatic drainage of the pharynx flows to retropharyngeal nodes and the upper deep cervical chain, especially the jugulodigastric node that enlarges with tonsillar infection and malignancy alike. Nasopharyngeal cancer classically presents through such nodes before nasal symptoms. **Bilateral drainage** above the hyoid explains contralateral nodes in midline tumours, shaping neck treatment fields even when one side feels clinically clear at presentation.
steps.say: Lymph drains to retropharyngeal and upper deep cervical nodes, especially the tonsil node under the jaw angle. Nasopharyngeal cancer often presents through neck nodes before nasal symptoms appear noticeably. Midline tumours drain bilaterally, which shapes neck treatment even when one side feels clear.

steps.tx: Applied anatomy closes with three bedside translations. Adenoid hypertrophy blocks the nasopharynx and tubal openings together, causing mouth breathing with ear effusion. Parapharyngeal tumours push the tonsil medially without mucosal ulceration, while retropharyngeal abscess bulges the posterior wall and threatens the airway. **Jugulodigastric enlargement** after sore throat is reactive until proven otherwise, but persistence in an adult demands nasopharyngeal examination and imaging.
steps.say: Enlarged adenoids block nose and ear tubes together, joining mouth breathing with ear effusion clinically. Side space tumours push tonsils inward under intact lining, unlike ulcerating mucosal cancers visibly. Persistent jaw angle nodes in adults demand nasopharyngeal inspection and imaging.

cards.b: Adenoid, paired tubal tonsils, paired palatine tonsils and lingual tonsil circling the pharyngeal entry.
Weak area between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus of inferior constrictor; pharyngeal pouches herniate through it.
External palatine vein over the tonsil capsule; classic source of primary post tonsillectomy haemorrhage.
